info.title: Brokerage REST API
info.summary: Accounts, positions, order status, transaction history, and stock and options trading.
info.description:
A resource-oriented REST API for retail and advisor brokerage integrations.

## Design contract

| Concern | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Style | Resource-oriented REST over HTTPS, JSON representations |
| Hypermedia | Every representation carries a `_links` map (see [HATEOAS](#section/HATEOAS)) |
| Authorization | OAuth 2.1 authorization code grant with PKCE (S256), optionally DPoP-bound |
| Errors | RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` |
| Money | Decimal **strings** plus an ISO 4217 currency, never IEEE-754 floats |
| Time | RFC 3339 timestamps, always UTC, always with an explicit offset |
| Pagination | Opaque forward cursors, surfaced as a `next` link |
| Safe retries | `Idempotency-Key` on every unsafe, non-idempotent operation |
| Concurrency | Strong `ETag` plus mandatory `If-Match` on order mutation |

## HATEOAS

Clients are expected to bookmark exactly one URL: the API root (`GET /`). Every
other URL in this API is discovered by following a link relation. Concretely:

* A representation's affordances live in `_links`, a map keyed by
  [IANA link relation](https://www.iana.org/assignments/link-relations/) or by a
  documented extension relation (`place-order`, `cancel`, `replace`, `positions`,
  `balances`, `transactions`, `executions`, `events`).
* `_links` is **state-dependent**. A `FILLED` order has no `cancel` link. An
  account without options approval has no `place-option-order` link. Clients MUST
  branch on the presence of a link rather than on a status string, and MUST NOT
  construct URLs by string concatenation.
* Each link carries `href` and, where the method is not `GET`, an explicit
  `method`. Templated links set `templated: true` and use RFC 6570 syntax.

## Versioning

The major version is pinned in the server path (`/v1`). Additive changes —
new fields, new enum members, new link relations — ship without a version bump,
so clients MUST tolerate unknown properties and unknown enum values rather than
failing closed.

## Out of scope

This document covers stock and options trading only. Futures, crypto, event
contracts, and the institutional application process are deliberately excluded.

get.description:
The hypermedia entry point. This is the only URL a client should hard-code;
everything else is reached by following `_links`.

200.description: The root document with links to every top-level collection.

get.description:
Returns every account the presented access token is authorized to see.

The `accountId` returned here is an opaque, permanent identifier. It is
**not** the account number the customer sees on statements — that value is
returned separately as `accountNumber`, masked unless the token carries the
`accounts:read:full` scope.

The list is small and bounded (a customer rarely has more than a handful of
accounts), so it is returned unpaginated.

200.description: Zero or more accounts, newest first.

twoAccounts.summary: An individual margin account and a Roth IRA

place-order.title: Place a stock or option order

get.description: Retrieve a single account by its opaque identifier.

200.description: The account resource.

get.description:
Cash, buying power, margin, and net liquidation value for one account.

Balances are a **snapshot**, stamped with `asOf`. Intraday they reflect
real-time marks on open positions and unsettled trade activity; after the
close they settle to end-of-day values. Do not cache beyond `Cache-Control`.

`buyingPower` is broken out by what it can be spent on, because the numbers
genuinely differ: a margin account's stock buying power is typically twice
its option buying power, and day-trading buying power is a separate,
larger number that resets each session.

200.description: A balance snapshot in the account's base currency.

get.description:
Open positions on the account, one row per instrument and side.

Long and short exposure in the same underlying are returned as separate
positions. Option positions carry the full contract descriptor and are
quantified in **contracts**, not shares; `contractMultiplier` (normally 100)
tells you how to convert.

Closed positions are not returned here — use the transaction history for
realized activity.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Restrict to one underlying symbol. Matches option positions on that underlying too.

200.description: A page of open positions.

mixed.summary: A long stock position and a short call against it

200.description: A single open position.

get.description:
Cash and position activity on the account: trades, dividends, interest,
fees, transfers, assignments, exercises, expirations, and corporate actions.

Results are ordered by `tradeDate` descending, then by `transactionId`
descending as a stable tiebreaker. Because settlement can back-date an entry,
a transaction may appear in a page you have already read; reconcile on
`transactionId`, which is permanent and unique.

The window defaults to the last 90 days. `from`/`to` accept any range up to
7 years; ranges wider than 1 year are served from cold storage and may take
several seconds.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on trade date. Defaults to 90 days ago.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on trade date. Defaults to today.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Restrict to one or more transaction types. Repeat the parameter to OR them.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Restrict to activity in one symbol or its options.

200.description: A page of transactions, most recent first.

page.summary: A fill, a dividend, and a fee

200.description: A single transaction.

get.description:
Orders on the account, newest first.

With no filter this returns **working orders only** (`PENDING_NEW`, `NEW`,
`PARTIALLY_FILLED`, `PENDING_REPLACE`, `PENDING_CANCEL`) — the set a trading
UI needs on load. Pass `status` explicitly, or `status=ALL`, to widen it.

This is a polling endpoint with a 1-second minimum interval. For sub-second
updates use the [order event stream](#operation/streamOrderEvents) instead;
polling harder will earn a `429`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Restrict to one or more statuses. Repeat to OR them. The literal `ALL`
disables the default working-orders-only filter.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Restrict to one underlying symbol, including its option orders.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on `createdAt`. Defaults to 7 days ago.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on `createdAt`. Defaults to now.

200.description: A page of orders.

post.description:
Submit a stock or option order. The request body is a discriminated union on
`assetClass`: `EQUITY` for single-leg stock and ETF orders, `OPTION` for
single- and multi-leg listed option orders.

### Idempotency is mandatory

`Idempotency-Key` is **required**. Send a fresh UUIDv4 per order intent and
reuse it verbatim on every retry of that same intent.

* First call with a key: the order is created, `201` is returned.
* Replay with the same key **and an identical body**: the original order is
  returned with `200` and `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. No second order.
* Replay with the same key and a **different** body: `422` with
  `type: .../idempotency-key-reuse`. Nothing is created.

Keys are retained for 24 hours. Without this, a socket timeout on a market
order is indistinguishable from a rejection, and the natural retry doubles
the customer's position.

### Order of operations

The service validates in this order and stops at the first failure, so a
rejection tells you the *first* thing wrong, not every thing:
schema → instrument tradability → market/session eligibility →
options approval level → buying power and margin → risk limits → route.

### Response is an acknowledgement, not a fill

`201` means the order was accepted and routed. It does **not** mean it
executed. Terminal state arrives via the event stream, a webhook, or by
polling the order resource.

equityMarketSell.summary: Stock — market sell to flatten a position

equityTrailingStop.summary: Stock — trailing stop 5% below the high

equityBracket.summary: Stock — entry with an attached profit target and stop (OCO exit)

optionSingleLeg.summary: Option — buy 5 AAPL Dec-26 250 calls to open, limit 12.40

optionVerticalSpread.summary: Option — 10 AAPL Dec-26 250/260 call debit spreads, net 3.15

201.description:
The order was created. `Location` points at the new order resource.
Check `status` — an order can be accepted and then immediately rejected
by the venue, which surfaces as a later `REJECTED` state, not as an
error on this call.

Location.description: Canonical URL of the created order.

200.description:
This exact `Idempotency-Key` and body were already processed. The
original order is returned unchanged and nothing new was created.

403.description:
The grant lacks `orders:write`, or the account is not approved for this
trade — most often an options strategy above the account's approval level.

value.title: Options approval level insufficient
value.detail: Selling uncovered calls requires LEVEL_4; this account is approved for LEVEL_3.

409.description: The account is restricted, or a conflicting order is already working.

422.description:
The body parsed and the schema validated, but the order cannot be
accepted: insufficient buying power, a price outside collar limits,
a closed market for the requested session, an untradable instrument,
or an idempotency key reused with a different body.

value.title: Insufficient buying power
value.detail: Order requires 123,750.00 USD of stock buying power; 84,360.20 USD available.

marketClosed.summary: Session not open for this order

value.title: Market closed
value.detail: Regular session is closed. Resubmit with extendedHours=true or timeInForce=GTC.

idempotencyConflict.summary: Key reused with a different body

value.title: Idempotency key reused with a different payload
value.detail: Key 6f1c2a90-... was first used for a 300-share order; this request is for 500 shares.

post.description:
Run an order through the full validation and pricing pipeline **without**
routing it. Same request body as [`placeOrder`](#operation/placeOrder).

Returns estimated cost, commissions and regulatory fees, the buying-power
impact, margin requirement, and any warnings the customer should see before
confirming. Use it to power a confirmation screen.

This operation is safe in the sense that matters — it never creates an order —
but it is modelled as `POST` because the request body is large and structured.
It is not cacheable and takes no `Idempotency-Key`.

200.description: Estimated economics and warnings. No order was created.

preview.summary: Preview of a marginable equity buy

warnings.message: This order exceeds available stock buying power by 39,389.80 USD.
After this order, MSFT would be 67% of account equity.

get.description:
A Server-Sent Events stream of order lifecycle transitions and executions
for the account. Prefer this over polling `listOrders`.

The stream replays from `Last-Event-ID` when the client reconnects, so no
event is lost across a dropped connection as long as you reconnect within the
5-minute retention window. Heartbeat comments arrive every 15 seconds; treat
45 seconds of silence as a dead connection and reconnect.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Resume the stream immediately after this event id.

200.description: An open `text/event-stream` connection.

id.description: Monotonic event id. Pass back as `Last-Event-ID` to resume.

get.description:
The current state of one order, including fills to date and the average fill
price. Responds with a strong `ETag`; send it back as `If-None-Match` to poll
cheaply and get `304` when nothing has changed.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Conditional GET. Returns `304` when the order is unchanged.

200.description: Current order state.

304.description: The order has not changed since the supplied `ETag`.

patch.description:
Amend a working order in place. Only `quantity`, `limitPrice`, `stopPrice`,
`trailingAmount`, `trailingPercent`, `netPrice`, `timeInForce`, and
`goodTilDate` may be changed — an amendment that would alter the instrument,
side, or leg structure is a different order and must be cancelled and
replaced explicitly.

`If-Match` with the order's current `ETag` is **required**. This closes the
race where you read an order, decide to reprice it, and it fills before your
amendment lands: the `ETag` will have moved and you get `412` instead of
silently amending an order that no longer exists in the state you assumed.

Amendment is best-effort against a live venue. A `200` means the amendment
was accepted for routing; the order may still fill at the old price if the
fill was already in flight.

reprice.summary: Move the limit up and shrink the order

extend.summary: Convert a day order to good-til-cancelled

200.description: The amended order. Note the new `ETag`.

409.description: The order is in a terminal state, or an amendment is already pending.

value.title: Order is not amendable
value.detail: Order ord_01HQ9D4N7Q1S5U8X is FILLED and can no longer be modified.

delete.description:
Request cancellation of a working order.

Cancellation is a **request**, not a guarantee. The order moves to
`PENDING_CANCEL` and reaches `CANCELLED` only once the venue acknowledges.
If a fill was already in flight the order may still reach `FILLED`, or
`PARTIALLY_FILLED` with the remainder cancelled. Always confirm terminal
state from the order resource or the event stream.

`If-Match` is required, for the same reason it is on `PATCH`.

This operation is idempotent: cancelling an already-cancelled order returns
`200` with the cancelled order rather than an error.

200.description:
The cancel was accepted. `status` will be `PENDING_CANCEL` — or
`CANCELLED` if the venue acknowledged synchronously.

409.description: The order already reached a terminal state other than `CANCELLED`.

get.description:
Individual fills against an order, oldest first. A single order can fill in
many prints across venues; this is the audit trail behind
`filledQuantity` and `averageFillPrice`.

200.description: All fills recorded against the order.

get.description:
Resolve a symbol or name to a tradable `instrumentId`. Covers listed equities
and ETFs. Use the option chain endpoint for option contracts.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Ticker or company name fragment. Minimum 1 character.

200.description: Instruments matching the query, best match first.

Cache-Control.description: Instrument metadata is stable; cached for 1 hour.

query.description:
A safe, idempotent search that takes a structured filter in the request
body. Semantically identical to `GET /instruments` but able to express
filters that will not fit in a URL.

Browser `fetch()` cannot issue a QUERY request. Clients on such stacks
should `POST` the identical body to `/instrument-screener` instead.

200.description: Instruments matching the structured filter.

post.description:
Compatibility alias for [`QUERY /instruments`](#operation/queryInstruments),
for clients that cannot issue a QUERY request — notably browser `fetch()`.
Identical request and response bodies.

Despite the `POST`, this operation creates nothing and has no side effects.
Responses are marked `Cache-Control: no-store` because `POST` responses are
not reliably cacheable; if caching matters, use QUERY.

200.description: Instruments matching the structured filter.
Instrument metadata including tradability flags.

get.description:
Listed option contracts on an underlying, with the `instrumentId` you need in
an order leg. Always narrow with `expiration` — an unfiltered chain on a
liquid name is thousands of contracts.

200.description: Matching option contracts.

post.description:
Delivered when an order transitions state or receives a fill. Signed with
`Webhook-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body, keyed by your webhook
secret) — verify it before trusting the payload, and compare in constant time.

Return `2xx` within 5 seconds. Non-2xx and timeouts are retried with
exponential backoff for 24 hours. Delivery is at-least-once, so handlers must
be idempotent on `eventId`.

200.description: Receipt acknowledged; the event will not be retried.

oauth2.description:
OAuth 2.1 with mandatory PKCE. Only the authorization code grant is
supported for user-facing applications; the implicit and resource owner
password credentials grants are removed by OAuth 2.1 and are not offered
here at any tier.

Access tokens are JWTs signed with RS256, valid for 15 minutes. Refresh
tokens are opaque, rotate on every use, and are valid for 90 days of
inactivity. Reuse of a rotated refresh token is treated as theft: the entire
token family is revoked immediately.

Public clients (mobile, SPA, CLI) MUST use PKCE with `S256` and MUST NOT ship
a client secret. Confidential clients SHOULD additionally use
`private_key_jwt` client authentication.

High-assurance integrations SHOULD request DPoP-bound tokens (RFC 9449), which
makes a stolen bearer token useless without the corresponding private key.

scopes.accounts:read: Read the account list and account metadata.
scopes.accounts:read:full: Read unmasked account numbers. Requires additional review.
scopes.positions:read: Read open positions, cost basis, and unrealized P&L.
scopes.orders:read: Read order status, order history, and executions.
scopes.orders:write: Place, amend, and cancel stock and option orders.
scopes.instruments:read: Search instruments and read option chains.
scopes.offline_access: Receive a refresh token for long-lived background access.

scopes.accounts:read: Read the account list and account metadata.
scopes.positions:read: Read open positions, cost basis, and unrealized P&L.
scopes.orders:read: Read order status, order history, and executions.
scopes.offline_access: Receive a refresh token for long-lived background access.

dpop.description:
Sender-constrained access tokens per RFC 9449. Send the access token as
`Authorization: DPoP <token>` together with a `DPoP` proof JWT bound to the
request method and URI. Required for `orders:write` on accounts above the
institutional risk threshold; recommended for everyone else.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description:
Opaque forward cursor from the previous page's `next` link. Do not construct
or parse it; its encoding is not part of the contract.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
A client-generated UUIDv4 that uniquely identifies this order intent.
Reuse it verbatim on every retry. Retained 24 hours.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description:
The `ETag` from your most recent read of this order. Required — a mutation
without it is rejected with `428 Precondition Required`.

ETag.description: Strong validator for the resource. Feed back as `If-Match` or `If-None-Match`.

IdempotencyReplayed.description: Present and `true` when the response was served from the idempotency cache.

RateLimit.description:
Remaining quota for the active window, per RFC 9913. Example:
`"default";r=94;t=51`.

RateLimitPolicy.description: The quota policy in force. Example: `"default";q=120;w=60`.

Problem.description: An unexpected error, described as RFC 9457 problem details.

BadRequest.description: The request was syntactically invalid or failed schema validation.

errors.detail: Must be a positive decimal string.

Unauthorized.description:
The access token is missing, malformed, expired, or revoked. The
`WWW-Authenticate` header names the failure. Refresh and retry once; if the
refresh also fails, send the user back through authorization.

Forbidden.description:
Authenticated, but not permitted. Either the grant lacks the required scope,
or the token is valid for a different account than the one addressed.

value.title: Insufficient scope
value.detail: This operation requires the orders:write scope.

NotFound.description:
No such resource, or the resource exists but is outside this grant. The two
are deliberately indistinguishable so the API cannot be used to enumerate
account identifiers.

PreconditionFailed.description:
The supplied `If-Match` does not match the resource's current `ETag` — the
order changed after you read it. Re-read it, decide again, and retry.

value.title: Stale order version
value.detail: The order was filled after you read it; your If-Match is stale.

PreconditionRequired.description: The mutation was rejected because no `If-Match` header was supplied.

UnprocessableOrder.description: The request was well-formed but the order cannot be accepted.

TooManyRequests.description:
Rate limit exceeded. Back off for `Retry-After` seconds, then retry with
full jitter. Repeatedly ignoring `Retry-After` escalates to a temporary
client suspension.

Decimal.description:
A fixed-point decimal carried as a string. Prices, quantities, and money are
never JSON numbers in this API: IEEE-754 doubles cannot represent `0.1`
exactly, and a rounding error in a share count or a limit price is a real
financial defect. Parse into a decimal type — `BigDecimal`, `decimal.Decimal`,
`Big.js` — never into a `float` or a JavaScript `number`.

Money.description: An amount paired with its currency.

Link.description:
One hypermedia affordance. The relation name is the key in the enclosing
`_links` map.

href.description: Target URI. RFC 6570 template when `templated` is true.

method.description: HTTP method to use. Absent means `GET`.

title.description: Human-readable label, safe to render in a UI.

templated.description: True when `href` is an RFC 6570 URI template.

type.description: Expected media type of the target.

Links.description:
Available affordances, keyed by link relation. **State-dependent** — a link
that is absent is an action that is not currently permitted. Branch on
presence, do not build URLs by hand.

Problem.description:
RFC 9457 problem details. `type` is a stable, dereferenceable URI and is the
only field safe to branch on — `title` and `detail` are human-facing prose and
may be reworded without notice.

type.description: Stable URI identifying the problem class. Branch on this.

title.description: Short human-readable summary. Do not parse.

status.description: HTTP status code, repeated for convenience.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.

instance.description: URI reference identifying the specific occurrence.

traceId.description: Correlation id. Quote this in every support request.

errors.description: Field-level failures, present on validation problems.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the offending field.

AccountType.description:
`CASH` settles trade-by-trade and cannot borrow. `MARGIN` can borrow against
equity, which changes buying power, short-sale eligibility, and the option
strategies the account may use.

AccountStatus.description:
`RESTRICTED` accounts can read but not trade — typically a compliance hold or
an unmet margin call. Trading operations on a restricted account return `409`.

OptionsLevel.description:
Approved option strategies, cumulative:
`LEVEL_1` covered calls and cash-secured puts ·
`LEVEL_2` long calls and puts ·
`LEVEL_3` spreads and other defined-risk multi-leg strategies ·
`LEVEL_4` uncovered (naked) short options.

accountNumber.description:
Customer-facing account number, masked to the last four digits unless the
grant carries `accounts:read:full`.

dayTrader.description: True when flagged as a pattern day trader, which imposes the 25,000 USD minimum equity rule.

asOf.description: When this snapshot was computed. Balances are not real-time streaming values.

netLiquidation.description: Total account value if every position were liquidated at current marks.

settled.description: Cash available without triggering a good-faith violation in a cash account.

buyingPower.description:
Broken out by use, because the numbers differ materially. In a margin
account `stock` is typically 2× `option`, and `dayTrading` is typically 4×
maintenance excess and resets each session.

marginBalance.description: Amount currently borrowed. Negative or zero when not borrowing.

marginCall.description: Present only when a call is outstanding.

dayTradesRemaining.description: Day trades left in the rolling 5-business-day window before the PDT rule bites.

occSymbol.description:
21-character OSI contract symbol: 6 chars root (space-padded),
6 digits `YYMMDD`, 1 char `C`/`P`, 8 digits strike × 1000.

contractMultiplier.description: Shares per contract. 100 for standard contracts; adjusted contracts differ.

InstrumentQuery.description: Structured screen, used with the `QUERY` method on `/instruments`.

expirations.description: Every expiration listed on this underlying, for building a picker.

quantity.description:
Signed. Negative for short positions. Shares for equities, **contracts**
for options — multiply by `contractMultiplier` for share-equivalent exposure.

subType.description:
Narrower classification within `type` — `BUY`, `SELL`, `SELL_SHORT`,
`BUY_TO_COVER`, `CASH_DIVIDEND`, `MARGIN_INTEREST`, `ACH_DEPOSIT`, and so on.
New values are added without a version bump; treat unknown values as opaque.

instrument.description: Absent for cash-only activity such as interest or transfers.

grossAmount.description: Signed from the account's perspective. Negative reduces cash.

netAmount.description: `grossAmount` net of `fees`. This is the cash movement.

OrderStatus.description:
Lifecycle state. Terminal states are `FILLED`, `CANCELLED`, `REJECTED`,
`EXPIRED`, and `REPLACED`; everything else is working. New members may be
added — treat an unrecognized status as working and rely on `_links` to know
what you may do with the order.

OptionSide.description:
Options are opened and closed explicitly. The open/close distinction drives
margin treatment and position netting, so it cannot be inferred from
buy/sell alone.

OrderType.description:
`NET_DEBIT`, `NET_CREDIT`, and `NET_EVEN` apply to multi-leg option orders and
price the combination as a whole rather than leg by leg.

TimeInForce.description:
`DAY` expires at the close · `GTC` persists across sessions (typically capped
at 90 days) · `GTD` requires `goodTilDate` · `IOC` fills what it can
immediately and cancels the rest · `FOK` fills entirely and immediately or
cancels · `OPG` participates in the opening auction only · `CLS` the closing
auction only.

PriceEffect.description: Whether the net price is paid or received. Required on multi-leg option orders.

OptionStrategy.description:
Declaring the strategy lets the risk engine apply spread margin instead of
naked margin on each leg — which is usually the difference between an order
being accepted and being rejected for buying power. `CUSTOM` is accepted but
margined leg by leg.

instrumentId.description: Option contract identifier, from the option chain.

ratio.description:
Contracts of this leg per unit of `quantity`. A 1×2 ratio spread uses
ratios 1 and 2.

Bracket.description:
Exit orders attached to an entry. They are released only when the entry
fills, and are mutually one-cancels-the-other: whichever triggers first
cancels the other.

EquityOrderRequest.description: A single-leg stock or ETF order.

clientOrderId.description:
Your own identifier, echoed on the order and every execution. Useful for
reconciliation; not a substitute for `Idempotency-Key`, which is what
actually prevents duplicates.

quantity.description:
Positive share count. Fractional quantities are accepted only on
instruments where `fractionable` is true, and only for `MARKET`/`DAY`.

trailingAmount.description: Absolute trail for trailing stops. Mutually exclusive with `trailingPercent`.

trailingPercent.description: Percentage trail for trailing stops. Mutually exclusive with `trailingAmount`.

extendedHours.description:
Route in the pre-market and post-market sessions. Extended-hours orders
must be `LIMIT` and `DAY`; spreads are wider and liquidity is thinner.

OptionOrderRequest.description:
A single- or multi-leg listed option order. Multi-leg orders are priced and
routed as one unit — legs never fill independently.

quantity.description:
Number of **strategy units**, not total contracts. A `quantity` of 10 on a
two-leg vertical is 10 spreads — 20 contracts — with each leg scaled by
its `ratio`.

netPrice.description:
Per-unit net price for the whole combination. Always positive; the
direction of the cash flow is carried by `priceEffect`, not by a sign.
Required for `NET_DEBIT` and `NET_CREDIT`.

OrderAmendment.description:
JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386) body. Only the listed fields are amendable.
An explicit `null` clears an optional field.

quantity.description: New total quantity. Must be at least the quantity already filled.

venue.description: ISO 10383 MIC of the executing venue.

liquidity.description: Whether the fill added or removed liquidity. Null when the venue does not report it.

side.description: Present on single-leg orders. Multi-leg orders carry per-leg sides instead.

legs.description: Present on option orders, including single-leg ones.

valid.description:
False when at least one warning has severity `ERROR`. Submitting an
invalid preview will be rejected — surface the warnings instead.

estimatedCost.description: Cash required. Null on orders that generate proceeds rather than cost.

estimatedProceeds.description: Cash generated. Null on orders that cost rather than generate.

maxLoss.description: Defined-risk option strategies only. Null when the downside is unbounded.

maxGain.description: Null when the upside is unbounded, as on a long call.

OrderEvent.description: One order lifecycle event, delivered over SSE or webhook.

eventId.description: Unique per event. Deduplicate on this — delivery is at-least-once.

order.description: Full order snapshot at the time of the event.
